metadata.title: What's justifying SpaceX's $2T valuation target ahead of IPO?

content.text:
According to Reuters, SpaceX (SPAX.PVT) is gunning for an IPO date of Friday, June 12, with hopes to begin trading on the Nasdaq at $135 per share. This could launch the value of Elon Musk's private space operator to $2 trillion.
Yahoo Finance Senior Reporter Pras Subramanian lays out the most valuable segments of the space company that Wall Street is watching.
Those numbers, by the way, that would imply a valuation of nearly 2 trillion dollars. What do you think what what is what would a bull say justifies that valuation? Is it Starlink? It's the launch business, it's the mythology of Musk, maybe it's all three.
Yeah, I think I think you nailed it. I think it's I think it's all three. I think it's the big things are in no particular order, right? The the rocket launch business right there that they're the premier payload provider to to space, right?
But low Earth and low Earth and regular orbit, right? Uh, they can do that at a at a cost that no one really can meet at this point from a private rocket company point of view.
That builds that business is ramping up. Starlink already making a ton of money, right? Uh, we're going to talk about this later, but it's a competitor in the broadband space, right? It's it's it's making it cost effective.
It's making it available throughout the globe. It's a an amazing product and used for both commercial, residential, you name it, right? Uh, and then finally the AI stuff. That's the part that people are getting tripped up on, right?
What does this mean? Orbital data centers, are you kidding me? This is going to be this is a thing, this is actually going to happen. If it does happen, then it that's part of your bull case. If it doesn't, it's sort of a kind of a a cost loss there for that business. What do you do there? Well, we have Colossus.
We have other AI products. We're going to push that. Uh it's going to feed Optimus's brain. you know, Tesla might become, you know, is is is part of this world, right? So, that's you're all sort of betting on this huge Musconomy thing that we talk about.
Uh, but in SpaceX, it's such a aspirational thing for investors and for just for for human civilization. I think that's why there's so much pent up sort of uh enthusiasm for this stock.
You know, Musk has never been a big fan of like Wall Street norms, Wall Street rules, right? Does his own thing. Are you already seeing examples of that in this in this SpaceX public debut?
You're seeing I think you're seeing it in some a little bit of pushback on on the street, right? We saw morning start to talk about how actually the valuation from my point of view is half what what he what they think it's going to be. Um, with that said, it's still an interesting company.
Don't buy it during IPO day, or the public offering day, buy it later when you get it cheaper. You know, there's so many different most initial public offerings, the stock within the first year is down like half.
saying go buy it then. So, you're not seeing Musk, you know, yeah, Musk is doing his thing no matter what. You you're either in, you're not. But Wall Street is sort of some of these banks are talking about how we agree with the business, we we're fans of Elon Musk, but this this is too rich right now. Especially the governance concerns, things like that.
You might see some pension funds not actually think about we don't want to be a piece of that. But I saw I saw, you know, Sam Rose talked about this today, our our our good friend. You know, are there any S&P tracking ETFs or indices that can do X space, right? Say X SpaceX because it's going to be such a big part of the industry.
Uh finally, you you mentioned this a second ago, but just to revisit, the analysts at Oppenheimer, they downgrade AT&T to perform. So basically it's the equivalent of a hold there. They move to the sidelines, and they they're talking about the SpaceX IPO there.
Yeah. Uh, you know, it's funny because I see AT&T is one of the most boring companies alive, right? Um, does the analyst need a reason to downgrade the stock? Is that what we're talking about here? But but I think, but analyst brings the fact that hey,
part one, Starlink is a true competitive threat to legacy broadband. Like I said, they can bring basic broadband anywhere without the massive buildout cost. So that's one thing. Um, AT&T's talking about AT&T's fiber buildout, again these high cost, high capital intensive uh uh offerings. Uh
the buildout is disappointing. They might they're tracking 60 million uh buildouts, but they might do 50 million. You know, there's there's a lot of bearishness on that legacy broad broadband business. Analysts like in particular Verizon and T-Mobile because they have less broadband exposure. So you're right.
Broadband might be getting its cake eaten by by Starlink.
